content.text:
The logo now returns HTTP 200 instead of the 307 redirect to `/login`.

Here is a summary of both fixes:

---

**Issue 1: JSON parse error on login** -- Fixed in `C:\Users\SKKU\Downloads\codex\recruiting_page\components\login-form.tsx`

Added `.catch(() => ({}))` to the `response.json()` call on line 27, matching the defensive pattern used throughout the rest of the codebase (e.g., `admin-request-sheet.tsx`, `candidate-management-table.tsx`, `procedure-detail-shell.tsx`). This prevents the raw browser error "Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input" from surfacing when the API response is empty or non-JSON (e.g., due to a server-side crash returning HTML), and instead shows the user-friendly fallback message.

**Issue 2: Logo not showing** -- Fixed in `C:\Users\SKKU\Downloads\codex\recruiting_page\proxy.ts`

The root cause was the Next.js proxy/middleware in `proxy.ts`. It intercepted ALL requests (except `/_next`, `/favicon`, and `/api/auth/*`) and redirected unauthenticated users to `/login`. This meant that when an unauthenticated user visited the login page, the `<Image src="/logo_SKKU_colored.png" />` request was redirected to `/login?next=%2Flogo_SKKU_colored.png` (confirmed: HTTP 307). The logo file itself existed and was valid.

The fix adds a regex check to allow common static asset extensions (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.svg`, `.ico`, `.webp`, `.woff2`, etc.) to pass through without authentication. After the fix, the image returns HTTP 200 as expected.
